focus: Unicode edge cases in subject — emoji, CJK characters, RTL text, zero-width characters

info.title: BulkChannelMessageSendJob.parse_text does not strip NBSP or ZWC from subject
info.detail: BulkChannelMessageSendJob.parse_text uses .scrub and .gsub for placeholder substitution but does not call .gsub(/\u00A0/, ' ') or .gsub(/[\u200B-\u200D\uFEFF]/, ''). This means NBSP and zero-width characters pass through into the subject sent via bulk messaging. By contrast, render_template_message (single-send template preview path) does strip both. This is a pre-existing inconsistency — the same gap exists for the body field in parse_text.

info.title: CreateChannelMessageTemplate does not clean NBSP from subject (only body)
info.detail: CreateChannelMessageTemplate interactor (line 11) cleans NBSP from body via context.params[:body]&.gsub(/\u00A0/, ' ') but does not apply the same cleanup to subject. NBSP can persist in template subjects in the database. render_template_message cleans NBSP at render time, so this is mitigated for the preview/single-send path, but bulk and automation paths use separate parse_text methods.
info.pre_existing: partially — body cleanup is pre-existing; subject not being cleaned is new but follows the same pattern

info.title: NBSP inside {{placeholder}} braces crashes render_template_message (Mustache::Parser::SyntaxError)
info.detail: If a user pastes NBSP (\u00A0) inside the braces of a Mustache placeholder (e.g., '{{\u00A0CandidateFirstName\u00A0}}'), render_template_message crashes at line 818 (subject) or line 813 (body). The crash occurs because Mustache::Template.new() is called on the RAW template text (not the cleaned subject_prepared), and Mustache's parser treats the NBSP as illegal content inside a tag. The actual Mustache.render calls (lines 806-808) succeed because they use the cleaned subject_prepared string. Confirmed this is a PRE-EXISTING bug — the same crash occurs for body (line 813) with NBSP in body placeholder braces. The subject implementation correctly mirrors the body pattern.

info.title: Zero-width characters not stripped in parse_apply_response_text, CreateStageAutomationMessage.parse_text, or BulkChannelMessageSendJob.parse_text
info.detail: Only render_template_message strips ZWC (\u200B-\u200D, \uFEFF) from subjects. The other three text-processing paths (parse_apply_response_text, CreateStageAutomationMessage.parse_text, BulkChannelMessageSendJob.parse_text) do not. This is pre-existing — the same inconsistency exists for body handling.

summary: 0 HIGH findings. All Unicode edge cases (emoji, CJK, ZWC, NBSP) are handled correctly for the subject field. The subject implementation correctly mirrors the body patterns in render_template_message. Four INFO items noted — all are pre-existing inconsistencies between the different text-processing paths (render_template_message vs parse_text variants). The most notable is INFO-3: NBSP inside placeholder braces can crash render_template_message, but this is confirmed pre-existing (same crash for body) and is a Mustache parser limitation, not a bug introduced by the subject feature.
